name: Plunket
lede: Plunket is an old English word for a greyish blue, once used for common pale blue cloth and now mostly a curiosity.

sections.title: A common pale blue
sections.body:
Paterson defines plunket as a greyish blue [1]. Its earliest use in our books is medieval: Balfour-Paul reports that late fourteenth-century records at York show blues predominating from September to December, and that *plunkets*, described as common pale blue cloth, were still worn alongside blues and greens in spring [2]. So the word named a common pale blue cloth rather than a pigment [2].

In the dictionary's blue list it sits with [[periwinkle]] and [[sky-blue]] [1]. The related poilu-blue is the greyish blue of French infantrymen in World War I [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of museum paintings, a color near this swatch is present in 40 works, 0.17 per cent of the archive [3]. The earliest is a work of 1445, and the latest dates from 1914 [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
